author: a. n. mills
title: Rep. Richard Neal addresses Cinco de Mayo and reproductive health care rulings
text:
Rep. Richard Neal, a longtime U.S. Congressman representing Massachusetts’ 1st district, addressed several issues in recent posts on his official Twitter account, including commemorating Cinco de Mayo and commenting on developments regarding women’s reproductive health care.
On May 5, 2026, Neal marked the Cinco de Mayo holiday by posting: “¡Feliz Cinco de Mayo! Today, we honor the resilient spirit that defined the Battle of Puebla in 1862, and celebrate the rich culture, heritage, and contributions of Mexican Americans across the country.”
The following day, May 6, he posted two tweets referencing the status of mifepristone access in the United States. In one tweet he stated: “Four years after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, mifepristone has become a critical part of women’s reproductive health care. While I welcome the Supreme Court’s decision to restore nationwide access to mifepristone temporarily, we must continue standing up to”. He also shared a link for further reading: “Read more: https://t.co/oVu1hgI3x5”.
Neal’s comments come amid ongoing national debates about abortion rights and medication access following the Supreme Court’s reversal of Roe v. Wade four years ago—a decision that significantly altered legal protections for abortion across states.
Richard Neal has served in Congress since 1989 after succeeding Edward Boland and previously held office in the Massachusetts House of Representatives. Born in Worcester in 1949 and currently residing in Springfield at age 74, Neal is an alumnus of American International College with a Bachelor of Arts degree.
